Does the answer depend on the pooling method?

With two or three studies the Cochrane Handbook (10.10.4.4–10.10.4.5) asks for a sensitivity analysis comparing interval methods rather than a choice between them. Both are given here; the published interval is the first row.

Table 8. Does the answer depend on the pooling method?
IntervalMethodSummary (95% CI)
as publishedREML0.9074 (0.831 to 0.9908)
sensitivity (Handbook 10.10.4.5)REML with Hartung-Knapp, t on k-1 = 1 degree(s) of freedom (t = 12.7062)0.9074 (0.5132 to 1.6045)

The published point is 0.9074 and the house-rule point is 0.9074. The number a reader remembers does not move; what differs is the precision claim. That is why nothing downstream catches this -- every memorable quantity survives.

A floor of 1 is applied to the variance-inflation factor so the adjustment can never narrow an interval below the unadjusted one. That guard is the recognised modification for exactly this instability, and its existence is evidence the small-k behaviour is a known problem with known handling rather than a novel judgement.

This is recorded as a declared departure under Cochrane Handbook §III.3.4.1: the review reports a pooled estimate for which no certainty assessment was made. It records nothing about what that quantity was measured against -- whether the comparators are of one kind, whether each comparison was randomised, whether it was concurrent. ScopeNone. It reports the three trials side by side and does not pool.
The finding of this comparisonA published systematic review of these exact trials looked at them and did not pool them. Kluger et al. 2018 reported the three CVOTs side by side and concluded that matching inclusion criteria and endpoints would be needed 'to ensure a truly direct comparison of the drugs'. They name the difference: Empa-reg outcome required prior confirmed cardiovascular disease and enrolled 99.2% with CVD, against 40.6% in DECLARE-TIMI 58. This object pools those two populations into one odds ratio of 0.9074. The comparison therefore does not adjudicate our estimate -- it questions whether the pool should exist. Withdrawing or restating it is a content decision and is not made here.

Introduction

1Background. This review asks: In Multiple trial-declared outcomes: Time to the First Occurrence of Any of the Following Adjudicated Components of the Primary Composite Endpoint (3-point M | Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (mace) Composite of Cardiovascular (CV) Death, Non-Fatal Myocardial Infarction (MI), | Subjects Included in the Composite Endpoint of CV Death, MI or Ischemic Stroke | Time to First Occurrence of mace (Composite Endpoint of Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events [Cardiovascular Death, Non-f, what do the contributing trials show? It pools 2 randomised trials. The outcome pooled is Multiple trial-declared outcomes: Time to the First Occurrence of Any of the Following Adjudicated Components of the Primary Composite Endpoint (3-point M | Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (mace) Composite of Cardiovascular (CV) Death, Non-Fatal Myocardial Infarction (MI), | Subjects Included in the Composite Endpoint of CV Death, MI or Ischemic Stroke | Time to First Occurrence of mace (Composite Endpoint of Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events [Cardiovascular Death, Non-f.

[Draft] The evidence identified on this question is 2 randomised trials (NCT01131676, NCT01730534), pooled here at 0.907 (95% CI 0.831 to 0.991) for primary. Which of those unresolved points makes the question worth asking now is the author's judgement.2

Results

The pooled odds ratio for multiple trial-declared outcomes: Time to the First Occurrence of Any of the Following Adjudicated Components of the Primary Composite Endpoint (3-point M | Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (mace) Composite of Cardiovascular (CV) Death, Non-Fatal Myocardial Infarction (MI), | Subjects Included in the Composite Endpoint of CV Death, MI or Ischemic Stroke | Time to First Occurrence of mace (Composite Endpoint of Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events [Cardiovascular Death, Non-f was 0.907 (0.831 to 0.991) across 2 trials.1

This pool is referred, not withdrawn. The stroke component is not the same component. EMPA-REG's 3-point mace counts non-fatal stroke of any type; declare's counts ischemic stroke only. Haemorrhagic stroke is inside one composite and outside the other. Two different endpoints sharing a name. Declare registers two co-primaries and this review silently used one. The other -- CV death or hospitalisation for heart failure -- is at the same rank and is the endpoint on which declare was positive. An unrecorded selection among co-primaries is an unrecorded analytic decision. The obstacle is in the evidence. Withdrawing a published estimate is a published-number decision and belongs to Mahmood. The estimate is unchanged; the finding is complete and stated.2

Noted on this pool. A published synthesis of this question included 3 trials where this pool carries 2. Source: Kluger et al., Reviews in Cardiovascular Medicine 2018, PMID 31032602, 'Cardiorenal Outcomes in the canvas, declare-timi 58, and empa-reg outcome Trials'. The third trial is named: the canvas Program. It is in the title of the review and is not carried by this object. This is the only topic in the corpus where a trial we do not pool can be named. The estimate above is computed from the trials this object carries and is not withdrawn or altered by this note. What a reader is owed is the scope: a larger evidence base on this question exists in the literature, and whether this review's search should be widened is a decision that has not been made.3

The trials' results were closely consistent with one another: I-squared, the share of the variation between them that is more than chance alone would produce, was 2.27%; the estimated variance of the true effects between trials (tau-squared) was 0.000106, the heterogeneity test statistic Q was 1.02, on degrees of freedom 1.4

The grounds for pooling are recorded as: The extractor recovered a pooled result from this page, so the page pooled these trials. Whether they should have been pooled is not established by conversion - several pages in this corpus pooled harm with efficacy, or distinct agents, and their estimates were withdrawn for that reason. Where a later pool on this page rests on the same grounds, they are not restated.5

The full model output for every pooled outcome -- the call, the estimator, the heterogeneity statistics and the back-transformed interval -- is reproduced verbatim as Extended data at the end of this article, so every number above can be checked against the software that produced it.6

Discussion

[Draft] The pooled OR is 0.907 (95% CI 0.831 to 0.991) over 2 trials. Whether a change of that magnitude is clinically meaningful in this population is the author's judgement: no field on this object records a threshold of importance, and none is assumed here.1

[Draft] Across 2 trials, tau-squared 0.0001; 1 of the 2 trial intervals include no effect and 1 exclude it. Whether that degree of disagreement matters clinically -- whether the trials are answering the same question in the same patients -- is the author's judgement.2

[Draft] This review pools 0.907 (95% CI 0.831 to 0.991) over 2 trials. The appraised synthesis pooled none. It reports the three trials side by side and does not pool.. Which trials that synthesis carries: Both contributing trials are keyed to a verified registration -- NCT01131676 and NCT01730534 -- and the comparable review names both in its title, so the trial-set match is read rather than inferred. Why the two results differ -- whether by population, outcome definition, model or included set -- is the author's judgement.3

[Draft] The evidence base is 2 trials, with no risk-of-bias assessment recorded. Whether that is enough to answer the question depends on the decision the answer is for, which is not stated on this object, and is the author's judgement.4

[Draft] No GRADE assessment is recorded, so no downgrade reason is available. What further evidence would change the conclusion is a judgement about a trial nobody has run, and is the author's.5

Comparison with published syntheses

Published syntheses were identified as follows. PubMed E-utilities, executed 2026-08-20. Query, counts and per-record disposition in ssot/sglt2-mace-cvot-review/appraisal/PUBLISHED_SYNTHESIS_SCREEN.json. 313 records matched; Only 300 ids were returned because the request capped at 300, so 13 matched records were never listed and are not merely unread -- they were never seen. 300 summaries read, 4 flagged by title, 2 appraised against their abstracts, 296 not appraised.1

This review was compared against 2 published synthesis(es); the denominator is stated because a comparison against an unstated number of reviews is not a comparison.2

What this comparison found. A published systematic review of these exact trials looked at them and did not pool them. Kluger et al. 2018 reported the three CVOTs side by side and concluded that matching inclusion criteria and endpoints would be needed 'to ensure a truly direct comparison of the drugs'. They name the difference: Empa-reg outcome required prior confirmed cardiovascular disease and enrolled 99.2% with CVD, against 40.6% in DECLARE-TIMI 58. This object pools those two populations into one odds ratio of 0.9074. The comparison therefore does not adjudicate our estimate -- it questions whether the pool should exist. Withdrawing or restating it is a content decision and is not made here.3

On what basis their trial set is known: Both contributing trials are keyed to a verified registration -- NCT01131676 and NCT01730534 -- and the comparable review names both in its title, so the trial-set match is read rather than inferred.4
